newsitem.title: USA: Timken optimistic about second half of '97.
newsitem.headline: Timken optimistic about second half of '97.

text.p: The Timken Co said Tuesday that it remained optimistic about the rest of 1997, following the release of record second quarter earnings of $44.9 million, or $0.72 per share, on revenues of $676 million.
In a statement accompanying Timken's earnings report, chief executive Joseph Toot said, "As we look ahead, our product mix and our markets look promising for the remainder of the year.
"In spite of fluctuating passenger car schedules and softening markets in certain geographic areas, we remain optimistic."

He also noted that the company is benefiting from ongoing cost-cutting initiatives. "We have more than met our stated goal of $200 million in annual manufacturing cost savings based on 1993 volume levels," said Toot. "This is contributing to faster growth as well as better performance for shareholders and customers.
Timken is a manufacturer of steel and engineered bearings.
